title: The Creepiest Octopus at Every Depth, Down to 6,957 Meters
alt_titles: Why Octopuses Get Creepier All the Way Down to 6,957 Meters
Every Reason the Octopus Is the Ocean's Creepiest Animal
Why the Octopus Gets Creepier the Farther Down You Find It
Octopuses Punch Fish, and They Only Get Creepier From There
thumbnail_brief: One big red octopus fills the frame with one arm curled into a fist, tiny Doug floating in front of it in a goatfish costume (red cap on top), with the words IT PUNCHES, so the title gives the depth range (every depth down to 6,957 m) and the thumbnail shows the first shock at the top of it; eerie, not cute: no big sparkly eyes, no smile, no OCTOPUS, CREEPIEST, DEPTH or 6,957 on the image. Variant B: a pale dumbo octopus (fins, no mascot face) looking into the porthole of Doug's sub on a black trench floor, hull starting to dent, IT LIVES HERE. Variant C: a pale octopus mother wrapped over her eggs on a dark ledge, Doug on a folding stool beside her with a long cartoon beard and torn calendar pages, 53 MONTHS (the mother's fate is never drawn).
description:
Octopuses punch fish, impersonate sea snakes and throw shells at each other, and one deep-sea mother guarded her eggs for 53 months. Doug follows the octopus from a shallow Red Sea reef to the deepest octopus ever filmed, 6,957 meters down in the Java Trench, and it only gets creepier the deeper he goes.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe and watch Doug's death counter keep climbing.
